_what: THE AUTONOMY LOOP'S HEALTH BOARD, AS A FILE. The ten §5.2 conditions, when each was measured, how long it has been that way, and when this file should be considered dead. Written by research/autonomy/health.py.
_read_this_when: you want to know whether the unattended research loop is WORKING — not whether what it wrote is correct, which every preflight gate already covers (§5.1). A loop can be perfectly correct and advance nothing.
_this_channel_is_PULL_ONLY: nothing here sends, opens an issue, comments, or fails a run. §7 trigger 4 is the ONE push, and it is the caller's act, not this file's: a condition red past its deadline earns a PushNotification and a line in the Friday digest, nothing else.
_stale_window_basis: read from autonomy-state.json `cycle_interval_hours` = 4 h, which is its one home (the governor writes it — architecture §9.2). Not typed here.
_stale_after_means: IF THE CLOCK IS PAST THIS AND THIS FILE HAS NOT CHANGED, NOTHING IS CHECKING THE LOOP and every verdict below is a memory, not a measurement. The deadline is written INTO the artifact because a checker that has stopped cannot report that it stopped — it needs no process, no API and no clock but yours. 3 missed cycles at 4 h. Restart it: `gh workflow run autonomy-tick.yml --ref main`.
_ok_means: no condition is FAILING. ⛔ IT DOES NOT MEAN EVERY CONDITION WAS MEASURED — read `fully_measured` and `unmeasured` beside it. `ok: true, fully_measured: false` is the honest shape of a loop nobody can yet grade, and it is NOT a healthy loop.
_blocking_means: research-loop §1's stop condition. A red row that is NOT here is reported and escalated but must never stop the loop, because a cycle cannot act on it. On 2026-08-27 the distinction did not exist, every red stopped the loop, and two retrospective conditions about immutable committed history wedged it permanently.
_unmeasured_means: ⛔ A VERDICT THAT COULD NOT BE REACHED — NOT a condition that is fine. It is listed apart from needs_attention because the fix is different: make the reading possible first. CLAUDE.md §4: an absent reading is not a reading of absence. Anything that grades an unmeasured condition as green has manufactured a green board out of missing data.

conditions.label: is `main` green, so a cycle can even commit?
conditions.source: --gates-verdict (written by the workflow that can read Actions)
conditions.detail: no gate verdict was supplied. This checker has no network by design, so it cannot read Actions itself. Settle it: have the tick workflow write {"ok": bool, "red_since_utc": str|null, "detail": str} and pass it with --gates-verdict.

conditions.label: is a fired cycle actually DELIVERING a receipt?
conditions.detail: the last receipt (CYC-0029-crossfil.json) landed -0.2 h ago, inside the 8.0 h deadline.

conditions.label: are cycles moving LIVE routes, or just documenting?
conditions.detail: 3 of the last 3 cycles moved a live route (RT-IPD-SURVIVAL, RT-AUTONOMY, RT-CHAPERONE, RT-LIMB-PERFUSION, RT-LUNG-DIRECTED, RT-IPD-SURVIVAL, RT-AUTONOMY).

conditions.label: is work in flight producing new EVIDENCE, not just heartbeats?
conditions.detail: the ledger was read and no entry is in state `running`, so no entry can be frozen. Vacuously true, and stated as such: this row says the check ran, not that the loop is busy — `cycle_delivering` is the row that says that.

conditions.label: does every BLOCKED row carry the observation that blocked it?
conditions.detail: the ledger was read and no entry is in state `blocked`.

conditions.label: is there any work a cycle could actually pick up?
conditions.source: research/autonomy/research-ledger.json — unowned, unblocked, retry budget remaining

conditions.label: is each cycle getting a fresh context, or is one session doing all of them?
conditions.detail: 6 session(s), worst carries 1 cycle(s) against a cap of 2.

conditions.label: did any cycle fan out wider than the governed cap?
conditions.source: receipts' `subagents.max_concurrent` (name owned by research/autonomy/receipt_schema.py), against autonomy-state.json `subagent_width`
conditions.detail: 6 cycle(s) recorded a fan-out; the widest was 5 against a cap of 5.

conditions.label: is the budget governor RECOVERING, or stuck in backoff?
conditions.detail: the governor records backoff level 0 — the loop is running at full cadence and width.

conditions.label: did every OUTWARD act have a grant behind it?
conditions.detail: the authority file is present and no receipt records an outward act, so nothing went out unauthorised.

_commit_worthy_why: every verdict is unchanged and the committed board is not near its expiry — this run carries no information the last one did not
_commit_worthy_means: fleet_armed.py's discipline: the caller COMMITS this file only when this is true. A board whose verdicts are unchanged carries no information (measured cost of ignoring that: 1,476 commits in 24 h, 703 of them non-events), and the keep-alive clause makes sure a live checker can never be the reason the board looks dead.
